newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung to release handover celebration details.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung to release handover celebration details.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa expects to announce this week the details of planned celebrations to mark the territory's return to Beijing's control, a senior official at his office said on Monday.

Michael Suen made the comment after Tung met China's ruling State Council secretary-general Luo Gan in the south China city of Shenzhen on Monday over the planned celebrations for Hong Kong's reversion to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.

"Mr Tung met with Mr Luo Gan this morning in Shenzhen and they had a useful meeting, going through the future arrangement for the celebration activity of the night of the 30th (of June) and on the morning of the 1st of July," Suen told reporters.
"An announcement regarding the details will be made shortly," he said. "Within the week."
"There are still some details that we need to confirm," he said, explaining why an announcement could not be made on Monday.
Suen, who accompanied Tung at the Shenzhen meeting, declined to elaborate.
The post-colonial leader will take over from Governor Chris Patten when the British pull out at midnight on June 30, sparking celebrations on both sides of the border.

Britain and China have said they will stage a glitzy ceremony at midnight on June 30 at the new extension of the Hong Kong convention centre, attended by 4,000 dignitaries, including U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan.

Britain's heir to the throne, Prince Charles, will lead the British delegation. It is not clear who will be most senior Chinese official attending the ceremony marking the end of 156 years of British rule.
